channelTitle: Sleepy Hollow, 1820 - the teacher who rode home at midnight and never arrived - Part 1
hook: A schoolteacher rode home alone through the hollow one autumn night - what chased him is still America's most famous ghost.
storyParts: Washington Irving published the tale in 1820, set in a misty valley called Sleepy Hollow - a place so quiet, he wrote, that people there seemed to dream while awake.
The valley's darkest legend was a Hessian soldier who lost his head to a cannonball during the Revolutionary War - locals swore he rode out every night searching for it.
Into this valley came Ichabod Crane, a lanky, superstitious schoolteacher who loved ghost stories almost as much as he loved Katrina Van Tassel - the richest farmer's daughter.
But Ichabod had a rival: Brom Bones, the village prankster - strong, handsome, and famous for practical jokes that somehow always had a ghostly twist.
One October night at the Van Tassel harvest party, the guests traded Hessian stories until late - and old Brom told his own tale of racing the Headless Horseman to the church bridge... and winning.
cta: What met Ichabod on the road home that night? Part 2 is in the Headless Horseman playlist.
